paper.title: Learning to Optimize Via Posterior Sampling

settings.name_in_paper: Finitely many actions, rewards in [0,1], arbitrary prior (Bayesian regret)
unmapped: arbitrary prior over an arbitrary reward-function class; action rewards may be dependent
general formulation allows random time-varying available action subsets A_t
settings.definition_quote: If $|\mathcal{A}|=K<\infty$ and $R_t \in [0,1]$ ... we make no further assumptions on the class of reward functions $\mathcal{F}$ or on the prior distribution over $\theta$.

unmapped: general formulation allows random time-varying action sets A_t; proposition does not restrict them
settings.definition_quote: If $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $f_\theta(a)=\left\langle \phi(a), \theta \right\rangle$ ..., $\sup_{\rho \in \Theta} \|\rho\|_2 \leq c_1$, and $\sup_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \|\phi(a)\|_2 \leq c_2$, and for each $t$, $R_t - f_{\theta}(A_t)$ conditioned on $(H_t, A_t, \theta)$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized linear models with bounded rewards, Bayesian regret
unmapped: rewards in [0,C] for a fixed constant C (rescaled [0,1])
learner knows actions a_1..a_d with sum phi(a_i)phi(a_i)^T >= lambda I used for initial exploration
settings.definition_quote: If $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $f_\theta(a)=g(\left\langle \phi(a), \theta \right\rangle)$ for some strictly increasing continuously differentiable function $g$, ... $\mathcal{A}_t = \mathcal{A}$ for all $t$, $\sum_{i=1}^{d} \phi(a_i) \phi(a_i)^T \succeq \lambda I$ for some $a_1,\ldots,a_d \in \mathcal{A}$, and $R_t \in [0,C]$

settings.name_in_paper: Gaussian processes (finite action set, GP prior)
unmapped: reward function sampled from a Gaussian process prior (Bayesian GP bandit)
settings.definition_quote: If $\mathcal{A}$ is finite, $\left( f_\theta(a):  a\in \mathcal{A} \right)$ follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution with marginal variances bounded by $1$, ... $\{R_t-f_{\theta}(A_t)\}$ is an iid sequence of zero-mean Gaussian random variables with variance $\sigma^{2}$

settings.name_in_paper: General function classes (bounded reward functions, sub-Gaussian noise)
unmapped: reward function in a known arbitrary class F with f(a) in [0,C]
complexity measured by eluder dimension and Kolmogorov dimension
formulation allows random time-varying action sets A_t
settings.definition_quote: Assumption: For all $f \in \mathcal{F}$ and $a \in \mathcal{A}$, $f(a) \in [0,C]$. Assumption: For all $t \in \mathbb{N}$, $R_t-f_{\theta}(A_t)$ conditioned on $(H_t, \theta, A_t)$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian.

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized linear models (via eluder dimension), sub-Gaussian noise
settings.definition_quote: Consider the case of a $d$-dimensional generalized linear model $f_{\theta}(a):=g\left(\left\langle \phi(a),\,\theta\right\rangle\right)$ where $g$ is an increasing Lipschitz continuous function.

algorithms.name: Posterior sampling with initial designed exploration (pi^IPS_{a_1..a_d})

source.label: prop:finite
source.quote: If $|\mathcal{A}|=K<\infty$ and $R_t \in [0,1]$, then for any $T\in \mathbb{N}$ $\mathrm{BayesRegret}(T, \pi^{\mathrm{PS}}) \leq 2\min\{K, T\}+4\sqrt{K T(2+6\log(T))}$.

results.notes: Holds for arbitrary prior; distribution-independent Bayesian regret bound.

conditions: noise sigma-sub-Gaussian conditionally on (H_t, A_t, theta)

source.label: prop:linear
source.quote: Fix positive constants $\sigma$, $c_1$, and $c_2$. If $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $f_\theta(a)=\left\langle \phi(a), \theta \right\rangle$ ..., then ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) = O(d \log T \sqrt{T})$

results.notes: Derived from Abbasi-Yadkori et al. 2011 via regret decomposition; proof only sketched. Also recovered in Section 7 linear example (O(d sqrt(T) log T)).

symbols.E_sqrt_theta0_d_T: prior expectation of sqrt(||theta||_0 * d * T), where ||theta||_0 is the number of nonzero components of theta

results.notes: Sparse linear bound derived from Abbasi-Yadkori et al. 2012; expectation over prior inside the bound so encoded as a single symbol.

symbols.r: ratio sup g'(<phi(a),rho>) / inf g'(<phi(a),rho>) of maximal to minimal link slope

conditions: g strictly increasing and continuously differentiable
there exist a_1..a_d with sum phi(a_i)phi(a_i)^T >= lambda I

source.label: prop:generalizedLinear
source.quote: Fix positive constants $c_1$, $c_2$, $C$, and $\lambda$. If ... $R_t \in [0,C]$ for all $t$, then ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm IPS}_{a_1,\ldots,a_d}\right) = O(r d \log^{3/2} T \sqrt{T})$, where $r=\sup_{\rho,a}g'(\langle \phi(a), \rho\rangle) / \inf_{\rho,a}g'(\langle \phi(a),\rho\rangle)$.

results.notes: Derived from Filippi et al. 2010; proof sketched only.

conditions: GP prior marginal variances bounded by 1
noise iid zero-mean Gaussian with variance sigma^2, independent of (H_t, theta, A_t)

source.quote: If $\mathcal{A}$ is finite, $\left( f_\theta(a):  a\in \mathcal{A} \right)$ follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution with marginal variances bounded by $1$, ... then ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right)\leq 1+2\sqrt{T \gamma_T \ln\left(1+\sigma^{-2}\right)^{-1} \ln\left(\frac{(T^2+1) \left| \mathcal{A}\right|} {\sqrt{2\pi}} \right)}$ for all $T \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.notes: Proposition unlabeled; gamma_T is maximal information gain. sigma is the noise standard deviation.

symbols.C_f: uniform bound on reward functions, f(a) in [0,C]
symbols.beta_star: confidence parameter beta*_T(F, delta, alpha) = 8 sigma^2 log(N(F,alpha,||.||_inf)/delta) + 2 alpha T (8C + sqrt(8 sigma^2 ln(4T^2/delta)))

source.label: prop: Bayesian regret bound in terms of beta
source.number: Proposition (prop: Bayesian regret bound in terms of beta)
source.quote: For all $T \in \mathbb{N}$, $\alpha > 0$ and $\delta \leq 1/2T$, ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) \leq 1+ \left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C +4\sqrt{{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right) \beta^{*}_{T} \left(\mathcal{F}, \alpha, \delta \right) T}.$

results.notes: alpha, delta are analysis parameters, not algorithm inputs (PS unchanged). Paper swaps argument order of beta* here vs. definition.

bound.expression_latex: 1+\left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C+ 16\sigma \sqrt{  {\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F},  T^{-1} \right) \left(1+o(1)+{\rm dim}_K\left(\mathcal{F} \right) \right) \log(T) T}

symbols.C_f: uniform bound on reward functions, f(a) in [0,C]

source.label: prop: risk bound
source.quote: For any fixed class of functions $\mathcal{F}$, ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) \leq 1+\left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C+ 16\sigma \sqrt{  {\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F},  T^{-1} \right) \left(1+o(1)+{\rm dim}_K\left(\mathcal{F} \right) \right) \log(T) T}$ for all $T\in \mathbb{N}$.

results.notes: Specializes to O(d sqrt(T) log T) for linear models (Section 7 example).

symbols.C_f: uniform bound on reward functions, f(a) in [0,C]
symbols.N_F: cardinality |F| of the finite function class

source.label: prop: risk bound
source.quote: Further, if $\mathcal{F}$ is finite then ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) \leq 1+\left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C +8\sigma\sqrt{2{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right) \log\left(2\left|\mathcal{F}\right|T\right)T},$ for all $T \in \mathbb{N}$.

symbols.r: ratio of maximal to minimal slope of the link g over actions and parameters

conditions: g increasing Lipschitz continuous with slope bounded below and above

source.quote: Then, ${\rm dim}_K(\mathcal{F}) = O(d)$ and ${\rm dim}_E(\mathcal{F}, \epsilon) = O(r^2 d\log(r \epsilon))$ ... Proposition \ref{prop: risk bound} yields an $O(rd\sqrt{T} \log (rT))$ Bayesian regret bound.

results.notes: Stated in an example rather than a formal proposition; consequence of Prop (prop: risk bound) plus appendix eluder-dimension bound. Standard PS, no initial exploration.
